subject: Stakeholder lane coordination: model phasing windows and exemption lanes
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>
To: mina_haddad@redwood.example.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com, laura_bennett@redwood.example.com
Cc: ops-lead@acme-analytics.com
Date: 2028-06-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed deprecation windows + exception lanes for model family X

Team —

Quick note to start the day: Acme flagged the model-family-X sunset we discussed last week and asked for a concrete runway + exception lane process. I attached a working timeline (redwood-deprec-timeline-v1.pdf) and a current traffic snapshot from their side.

Key asks from Sales/CS (from Acme):
- A clear cutover date (we tentatively suggested 2028-08-01)
- A documented exception lane for customers who need a longer migration (30/60/90-day lanes)
- A comms cadence and who owns customer-facing notifications

Questions for Product/Infra:
1) Can we support a routing shim that maps the old endpoint -> variant model with parity for 30 days? If so, what are the perf/cost implications?
2) If we offer a paid extended runway, what gating checks do we need (QA evals, token quotas)?

I don't expect answers in this thread immediately, but want to capture owners. Suggested owners: Mina for roadmap asks and comms cadence, Karthik for routing shim feasibility, Ben for ops/runway pricing input, Laura for customer success playbook.

Attaching: redwood-deprec-timeline-v1.pdf, acme-traffic-snapshot-2028Q2.csv

Thanks —
Marissa
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.example.com, mina_haddad@redwood.example.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.example.com
Date: 2028-06-30T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed deprecation windows + exception lanes for model family X

Marissa,

Quick technical read: a routing shim is feasible as a short-term compatibility layer, but there are tradeoffs. Notes:
- We can implement a request-time route that translates calls from /v1/models/x to /v1/models/x-compat with a small header indicating compatibility mode. That buys us parity for stateless generation but breaks session-level KV cache continuity unless we also surface migration of session IDs.
- Perf: expect ~5-12% additional p95 latency for the shim under peak (depends on model variant and sequence length).
- Cost: the shim will stop benefiting from prefix-KV caching; you should budget extra token-cost and GPU-hours.

I'll need Ben to sanity-check the expected cost delta and Mina to confirm whether a temporary behavioral spec (where we accept slightly different sampling seeds) is acceptable for CS.

If Acme needs strict bit-exact parity we should mark that as a longer-term migration.

— Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.example.com>

Date: 2028-06-30T11:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed deprecation windows + exception lanes for model family X

Thanks for the summary, Marissa — good capture. I want to align on three practical outcomes we can commit to for Acme and to use as a template for similar customers:

1) Firm runway & canary: commit to the public sunset date of 2028-08-01, with a canary window starting 2028-07-10 for 20% of Acme's traffic (configurable). Canary will be opt-in for them in week 1, then we flip opt-out.

2) Exception lanes: offer three lanes — 30-day (no fee), 60-day (small professional-services fee), 90-day (PS + configurable support add-on). Each lane requires a minimal QA signoff checklist (see Drive checklist link) and a support SLA uplift for the longer lanes. Laura, please draft the customer playbook for how CS will present these lanes.

3) Routing shim & parity expectations: Karthik, the shim sounds ok as a temporary measure. We need explicit perf and quality SLAs documented for customers opting in. Ben, can you capture the expected cost uplift for each lane and a recommended surcharge?

Comms: I'll own the customer-facing announcement draft and will coordinate timing with Product Marketing. Suggested comms timeline:
- 2028-07-01: initial heads-up to customers at risk (Acme included)
- 2028-07-10: technical canary onboarding guide + API doc updates
- 2028-07-24: final reminder & migration resources
- 2028-08-01: cutover + post-cutover FAQ

Action items (owners & due dates):
- Laura: CS playbook draft (2028-07-05)
- Ben: cost uplift + surcharge recommendation (2028-07-03)
- Karthik: brief shim design doc with perf/caveats (2028-07-02)
- Marissa: confirm Acme interest in paid lanes (ASAP)
- Mina: announcement draft (2028-07-01)

If anyone thinks the public date should shift we should flag it now — otherwise let's proceed with the above.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Head of Product — Inference Platform
Redwood Inference

Drive checklist: https://drive.redwood.com/teams/migration/checklist-2028Q2
From: ops-lead@acme-analytics.com
To: mina_haddad@redwood.example.com, marissa_cole@redwood.example.com
Cc: platform-eng@acme-analytics.com
Date: 2028-06-30T13:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed deprecation windows + exception lanes for model family X

Mina / Marissa —

Thanks for the clear plan; Acme is generally aligned with the 2028-08-01 cutover but we have two constraints:
1) A compliance validation for our outputs that won't be complete until 2028-07-20 — that pushes our preferred canary start to 2028-07-22.
2) One of our teams requires session-level continuity for a subset of interactive users (they rely on long-lived KV cache behavior). If the routing shim breaks that we will need the 90-day lane.

We are open to the paid lane for the continuity requirement; please share the surcharge estimate and the QA checklist when ready. Also, confirm whether the shim will preserve user-visible tokens/session IDs or if we need to map them on our side.

Best,
Alex Rivera
Ops Lead, Acme Analytics
